findings.evidence: Spread candidates across distinct naming directions (compound, affix, evocative real word, coined blend)
findings.fix: Keep the one-pass screen (one spelling, unwanted meanings, nearby brands, word splits). Move the four naming-direction labels to references/example.md, which already groups by them, and record the move in docs/audit/recovery/domain-name-brainstormer/record.md.

findings.evidence: Procedure is a linear 1-7 list with no thinking prompt before generation or ranking
findings.fix: Add one expert prompt before step 2, in the skill's own terms: before generating, ask which word the user must say aloud, which meaning must never appear, and which existing brand the name must not sit next to.

findings.evidence: Gotchas covers 'available', prices, confusables and HSTS, but not the WHOIS no-record variants the procedure itself flags
findings.fix: Add one Gotcha: a WHOIS line that is not an explicit no-record reply (for example .mx Object_Not_Found wording the listed phrases do not name) stays unverified; only the replies named in step 5 count as not found in registry.

findings.evidence: description names .com, .io, .app, .dev and RDAP/WHOIS, but not the WHOIS-only TLDs the body treats specially (.co, .de, .es, .mx)
findings.fix: Brainstorm, screen and rank brandable domain names (.com, .io, .app, .dev, and WHOIS-only TLDs such as .co) for apps, products, companies and personal brands, and report registration status honestly via RDAP/WHOIS lookups. Use when naming a project, launching or rebranding, asking "is this domain available", or replacing a taken first choice, even if the user only describes the business. Not for DNS, email, hosting or transfers on a domain already owned, naming without domains, social handles, or legal trademark clearance.

findings.evidence: a budget cap (checked in step 6) are filters, not ranking weights. A name that fails one is cut
findings.fix: In step 1, say a budget cap filters only when the user supplied a registrar checkout quote; otherwise it is not a cut, and step 6's unverified budget-fit label is the only outcome.

Keep the exact curl invocation. Add one line: if the shell has no curl, use the same URL with the harness fetch tool and still apply the printed-result table; if that tool hides the status code or the final host, label the name unverified.

findings.evidence: expected_output: A set of relevant, pronounceable name candidates across suitable TLDs, with honest limits on live availability claims
findings.fix: Rewrite casual-climate-names expected_output to the procedure's actual product: assumptions stated, candidates grouped by naming direction, ranked table with pronunciation, rationale, risk, TLD fit, status label and RDAP URL, and a registrar-checkout close. Add one assertion that the table has those columns.

findings.evidence: Cut any candidate that has more than one plausible spelling when heard
findings.fix: Qualify the cut: drop a name with two equally likely spellings and no tie-breaker; keep a name whose intended spelling is the common one and record the rival spelling in the spelling-or-confusion-risk column, as the example does for snippetbox (snippit) and quillbin.

findings.evidence: devpaste.com status not found in registry, rationale Familiar from the pastebin habit
findings.fix: In the example, mark devpaste.com as cut or explain the tie-breaker, so the worked example does not keep a name step 2's 'more than one plausible spelling when heard' rule would remove.
